transactions.citation: FY2025 AR (p340-343): 'Divested Albany-Supermarket in January 2025 at 4.2% Above Purchase Price'. FY2024 AR (p1724): 'On 17 January 2025, UHREIT completed the divestment of Albany-Supermarket, New York. The divestment consideration of US$23.8 million is 4.2% higher than the purchase price of US$22.9 million.' FY2024 AR (p603): 'Subsequently in January 2025, we divested Albany-Supermarket in Albany County, New York, at 4.2% above its purchase price.'
transactions.notes: VERIFIED per user flag -- this is the RARE purchase_price basis (not book_value): the disclosed 4.2% is the divestment consideration of US$23.8m measured against the ORIGINAL ACQUISITION COST of US$22.9m: (23,800,000-22,900,000)/22,900,000*100 = 3.93%, which rounds imprecisely but is stated verbatim as '4.2%' by the REIT in both the FY2024 and FY2025 ARs (pct_source='disclosed', used verbatim per SPEC rule: 'If the AR states a percentage, use it verbatim'). reference_basis='purchase_price', reference_value=US$22,900,000 (the original purchase price, disclosed only in the FY2024 AR, p1724). SEPARATELY, and NOT to be confused with the 4.2%-above-purchase-price figure: an accounting LOSS on divestment of US$(684,000) was recognised in FY2025 (Statement of Total Return, p1482/5971/6127/7462), computed as net cash proceeds from divestment (US$23,116,000, Cash Flow Statement) LESS the 31-Dec-2024 balance-sheet CARRYING VALUE of US$23,800,000 -- i.e. (23,116,000-23,800,000)/23,800,000*100 = -2.87% loss against the held-for-divestment carrying value, which happened to equal the independent fair valuation as at 31 Dec 2024 (CBRE, Inc., US$23,800,000, per prior extraction p166/167 citations). These are two entirely different, both-genuine disclosures: (1) a 4.2% GAIN vs the property's decade-old original purchase cost of US$22.9m (the headline metric the Manager highlights), and (2) a small accounting LOSS of US$684k vs the most recent carrying/fair value of US$23.8m (the audited P&L line) -- because the property had appreciated in independent valuation well above its original cost by the time of sale, and the gross sale price landed almost exactly at that latest valuation, producing a small loss against carrying value even though it was a solid gain against original cost. Deal completed via a whole-property (100%) sale; interest_pct left null. Same deal_id used consistently across FY2024 and FY2025 filings per SPEC's cross-year-duplicate convention.

transactions.citation: p350-352: 'DPU-accretive Acquisition of Dover Marketplace in August 2025 at 4.8% Below Valuation'. p692: 'Announced the DPU-accretive acquisition of Dover Marketplace, a grocery-anchored property in Pennsylvania, on 1 August 2025. The purchase consideration of approximately US$16.4 million represents an ~4.8% discount to the independent valuation of US$17.2 million.' p1874: 'On 1 August 2025, UHREIT completed the acquisition of Dover Marketplace, a dominant grocery-anchored freehold property located in Dover Township, York County, Pennsylvania.' Portfolio valuation table (p1735): 'Dover Marketplace | 17,200 | - | N.M.' with footnote 3 (p1749): 'Dover Marketplace was acquired on 1 August 2025.'
transactions.notes: No gain/loss concept applies to an acquisition, so the five divestment fields are left null even though the AR explicitly discloses an acquisition-discount percentage (purchase consideration ~US$16.4m vs independent valuation of US$17.2m by Newmark Valuation & Advisory, LLC = ~4.8% discount, disclosed verbatim; cross-check (16.4-17.2)/17.2*100 = -4.65%, close to the disclosed ~4.8%). Third Pennsylvania asset; grocery-anchored (Giant/Ahold Delhaize), 9 tenants. Cash outflow for the acquisition (incl. acquisition costs) was US$17,046k per the Statement of Cash Flows -- a higher figure than the US$16.4m purchase consideration because it includes transaction costs; purchase_price recorded here is the pure purchase consideration (US$16.4m), not the all-in cash outflow, to keep it comparable to the disclosed valuation-discount basis.

transactions.counterparty: Seller not named; acquired via wholly-owned indirect subsidiary UH US Wallingford Fair 2025 LLC
transactions.citation: p358-361: 'DPU-accretive Acquisition of Wallingford Fair Shopping Center in January 2026 at 8.2% Below Valuation'. p1886: 'On 14 January 2026, UHREIT completed the acquisition of Wallingford Fair Shopping Center, a dominant grocery-anchored freehold property located in Wallingford. This acquisition represents UHREIT's maiden entry into Connecticut'.
transactions.notes: Subsequent-event acquisition: agreed and completed 14 Jan 2026, AFTER FYE 31 Dec 2025, but disclosed as completed by the time the FY2025 AR was issued -- status recorded 'completed'; deal_id year uses 2026 (the year the deal actually completed) per SPEC's cross-year convention. No gain/loss concept applies to an acquisition, so the five divestment fields are left null even though the AR explicitly discloses an acquisition-discount percentage (cash consideration US$21.4m vs independent valuation of US$23.3m by CBRE Valuation & Advisory Services as at 25 Nov 2025 = 8.2% discount, disclosed verbatim). Maiden entry into Connecticut; anchored by ShopRite, with Petco and an Extra Space Storage self-storage facility as the remaining two tenants (fully leased to three tenants total).
